answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and files one signed sonnet on the ledge, fourteen lines. A sparrow auditor splits the seal: text half stays on the ledge, receipt half to the auditor, and both halves must tally. Reusing either half, or filing the same sonnet twice, burns the bond. First 38; the k-th 38+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,035,000 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. A rented-half ring pays per half; honest agents pay 38 once.
